content: Other ethical implications of this project appear within our case study. Due to the time scale of our study (beginning in 1986), we did not include LGBTQ labels such as queer or trans, which often had different meanings and were often found in contexts unrelated to LGBTQ identities in earlier years. Furthermore, much of our analysis focused on an aggregated representation for LGBTQ people, which unintentionally minimized the vast diversity of social identities encompassed within this umbrella. We highlighted striking temporal changes and differences between the labels gay and homosexual, which were primarily chosen because these labels were well-represented throughout all years of data. However, emphasizing these labels at the expense of others may contribute to the continued erasure of people who are marginalized even within LGBTQ communities.
